expectations.text: The ADR states context, decision, alternatives, and consequences distinctly
expectations.evidence: Write tool created docs/decisions/ADR-001-event-sourcing-for-orders-service.md with separate headed sections: '## Status', '## Date', '## Context' (mutable rows, best-effort webhooks, auditor/support requirements, constraints), '## Decision' (append-only event stream + read projections), '## Alternatives Considered', and '## Consequences'. Each concern lives in its own section with no blending.

expectations.text: Trade-offs and rejected options are recorded, not just the winning choice
expectations.evidence: The Alternatives Considered section covers all three options from decision-context.md, each with Pros/Cons and an explicit 'Rejected:' rationale: the audit table is 'not the system of record [and] can silently diverge from actual state'; CDC 'Gives a technical changelog, not the business-level transition history'. The chosen option also lists its own Cons (projection rebuilds, event versioning, eventual consistency, operational complexity), and Consequences records the unresolved reporting-service synchronous-read conflict as 'the main integration risk'.

expectations.text: The document is written in timeless language describing current state
expectations.evidence: Context is written in present tense describing the system ('The orders service stores mutable order rows and emits best-effort webhooks'), not as a narrative of a meeting. The source file's 'Options discussed:' framing was converted into a standing 'Alternatives Considered' section. Decision is stated as a standing position ('Adopt event sourcing for orders: ... are persisted as ...') and Consequences describe resulting state ('Order reads served from projections become eventually consistent', 'Event versioning and upcasting are now a standing maintenance obligation'). No 'we met', 'last week', or 'will be changed' narrative.
